subject: social-studies
unit_title: Research Design and the Arc of Inquiry
title: Launch and diagnostic: compelling and supporting questions
essential_question: What makes a research question worth asking and actually answerable?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about compelling and supporting questions, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use primary and secondary evidence, maps, or data to communicate understanding of compelling and supporting questions.
Check, revise, or improve work about compelling and supporting questions using stated success criteria and source reliability.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about compelling and supporting questions.
The learner gives cited evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner distinguishes primary from secondary evidence and notes each source's perspective.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil or accessible response tool
unit source set retrieved from a named public repository
map, atlas, or data display appropriate to the unit

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “compelling and supporting questions.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Examine maps, data, and primary and secondary sources; establish provenance; contextualize competing perspectives; and support a historical, geographic, economic, or civic claim with cited evidence. Keep the explanation centered on compelling and supporting questions. Name the success criteria and model how to check a claim against its sources.

Complete two supported source-based or analytical tasks about compelling and supporting questions. After each step ask: “What evidence supports that move, and how do we know the source is reliable?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of compelling and supporting questions and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.

In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about compelling and supporting questions; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of compelling and supporting questions and records the result, the reasoning or evidence that produced it, and a citation for every source used.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about compelling and supporting questions; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, use and citation of evidence, fair representation of perspectives, and revision. Accept multiple valid interpretations when they meet the criteria and are supported by the sources. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

source_use.primary_secondary: Identify each source as primary or secondary, state who produced it and when, and note what perspective it represents and what it omits.
anchor_sources: C3 Framework for Social Studies State Standards (National Council for the Social Studies)
Michigan K-12 Social Studies Standards, Arc of Inquiry, grades 9-12 (Michigan Department of Education)
source_use.retrieval_note: Retrieve the actual text, map, or data from the named repository. This package names sources and never reproduces or paraphrases their wording as though quoted.

citation_requirement: Every claim offered as evidence names its source with enough detail for another reader to locate it. Quotations must be transcribed by the learner from the retrieved source; this package supplies no quoted text.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for compelling and supporting questions, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the reasoning for compelling and supporting questions works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of compelling and supporting questions, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Ask which source supports the claim and how it was corroborated. Do not supply the claim, the wording, or the citation.
Decline to draft or revise graded argumentative prose. Offer evidence analysis, questions, structure options, or feedback on the learner's own draft instead.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking compelling and supporting questions mastered.

tutor_boundary: The tutor may help locate, read, contextualize, and analyze evidence, and may question the learner's reasoning. The tutor may not draft, rewrite, or supply the wording of a graded argument, thesis, or citation. A static, tutor-free path through this lesson is always available.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use source analysis, map or data work, discussion, an evidence-based claim with citation, and an inquiry product; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two separate occasions.
extension: Apply compelling and supporting questions under a new constraint, compare two interpretations or regional perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, recorded, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media and maps.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Handle war, genocide, enslavement, oppression, displacement, identity, and belief with accurate context, documented evidence, and human dignity.
Do not require a learner to represent an identity or to argue for an injustice in simulation.
Represent contested issues with more than one well-sourced perspective rather than a single settled answer.

media.suggestion: Optional map, data display, timeline, document image, or short clip supporting compelling and supporting questions.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or printed model, or facilitator description.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of compelling and supporting questions in public life or local records. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about reflection and transfer beyond the course; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsupported claim, or an uncorroborated source.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, use and citation of evidence, fair representation of perspectives, and revision. Accept multiple valid interpretations when they meet the criteria and are supported by the sources. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

source_use.primary_secondary: Identify each source as primary or secondary, state who produced it and when, and note what perspective it represents and what it omits.
unit_source_focus: the learner's own annotated source dossier
public records relevant to the action
anchor_sources: The learner's annotated source dossier assembled in Unit 3
Public records and correspondence generated by the learner's civic action
source_use.retrieval_note: Retrieve the actual text, map, or data from the named repository. This package names sources and never reproduces or paraphrases their wording as though quoted.

citation_requirement: Every claim offered as evidence names its source with enough detail for another reader to locate it. Quotations must be transcribed by the learner from the retrieved source; this package supplies no quoted text.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for reflection and transfer beyond the course, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the reasoning for reflection and transfer beyond the course works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of reflection and transfer beyond the course, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Ask which source supports the claim and how it was corroborated. Do not supply the claim, the wording, or the citation.
Decline to draft or revise graded argumentative prose. Offer evidence analysis, questions, structure options, or feedback on the learner's own draft instead.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking reflection and transfer beyond the course mastered.

tutor_boundary: The tutor may help locate, read, contextualize, and analyze evidence, and may question the learner's reasoning. The tutor may not draft, rewrite, or supply the wording of a graded argument, thesis, or citation. A static, tutor-free path through this lesson is always available.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use source analysis, map or data work, discussion, an evidence-based claim with citation, and an inquiry product; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two separate occasions.
extension: Apply reflection and transfer beyond the course under a new constraint, compare two interpretations or regional perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, recorded, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media and maps.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Handle war, genocide, enslavement, oppression, displacement, identity, and belief with accurate context, documented evidence, and human dignity.
Do not require a learner to represent an identity or to argue for an injustice in simulation.
Represent contested issues with more than one well-sourced perspective rather than a single settled answer.

media.suggestion: Optional map, data display, timeline, document image, or short clip supporting reflection and transfer beyond the course.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or printed model, or facilitator description.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of reflection and transfer beyond the course in public life or local records. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
